old_description: At Up North Plastics, Inc., a subsidiary of Poly-America, we manufacture the highest quality silage bags, grain bags, and bunker covers. We are located in Cottage Grove, Minnesota.
about:
Up North Plastics, Inc., a subsidiary of Poly-America, operates from Cottage Grove, Minnesota. The company manufactures silage bags, grain bags, and bunker covers designed for agricultural feed storage.

The plant runs on what the company describes as state-of-the-art manufacturing equipment, processing premium-grade polyethylene resins into multi-layer films. An extensively trained quality control team performs continuous testing during production, supplemented by additional analysis in an in-house laboratory and on test farms across the United States. Finished goods move through an international distribution network supported by a fleet of more than 300 semi-trucks.

Primary customers include grain producers, beef and dairy operations, and feed managers who rely on airtight storage to preserve high-value forages and grains. The company’s grain bags are engineered to withstand the stress of dry grain, while its bunker covers combine a 2-mil Silage Shield™ layer with a 5-mil black-and-white outer layer for spoilage reduction.

Up North Plastics emphasizes two differentiators: puncture and tear resistance that exceeds foreign competitors’ products, and a service network of distributors and dealers backed by the large truck fleet to ensure bags arrive when and where they are needed.

name: Uranus Fudge Factory & General Store - Uranus Missouri
old_description: Lemon Iced Tea Fudge is our August Fudge of the Month. Limited time only.
about:
Uranus Fudge Factory & General Store began on July 2, 2015, when founder Mayor Louie Keen opened the original location on Historic Route 66 in St. Robert, Missouri. The concept was born from a dare to create a roadside destination that captured old-school Americana — fun, family, and a good laugh — and it quickly became a travel landmark halfway between St. Louis and Springfield.

The company produces fudge fresh by hand every day, offering 18 signature flavors such as pumpkin pie nut and lemon iced tea, alongside 80-plus apparel designs, snacks, and novelty gifts. Operations have expanded to three physical locations: the St. Robert flagship (with mini golf, a sideshow museum, ice cream, and the "World's Largest Belt Buckle"); Anderson, Indiana (opened 2022 off I-69 Exit 222, adding an 18-hole mini golf course and playground); and Richmond, Indiana (opened late 2024 at I-70 Exit 156B), a 15,000-square-foot mega-store featuring a vortex tunnel, animatronic dinosaurs, a vintage bi-plane, a shooting gallery, and a dog park. An e-commerce site ships orders over $75 free within the continental U.S.

The brand serves tourists, highway travelers, families, and gift shoppers across the Midwest and beyond, drawing visitors from around the world who want to say they've been to Uranus. The company cites more than 20,000 five-star customer reviews as evidence of its appeal.

name: Utah Solar Detach & Reset
old_description: Panel position and wiring documented before removal, so every reconnection is accurate and secure.
about:
Utah Solar Detach & Reset operates from Kearns, Utah, serving homeowners and contractors across the Wasatch Front. The locally owned company grew out of a roofing business, giving its founders firsthand experience with the intersection of roof work and solar arrays.

The company specializes in solar panel removal and reinstallation — often called detach and reset — for roof replacements, system maintenance, or upgrades. Technicians document panel positions and wiring before any removal, then follow structured diagnostic sequences to isolate faults before replacing components. Additional services include solar panel cleaning with output verification, critter guard installation, EV charger installation, battery troubleshooting, and solar monitoring setup. Work is performed from a brick‑and‑mortar office in Kearns, with crews traveling to Sandy, Salt Lake City, West Jordan, Taylorsville, Murray, Draper, and surrounding communities.

Primary customers fall into two groups: homeowners who discover their solar arrays must be temporarily removed for roof repairs, and roofing contractors who need a reliable solar detach partner to keep their projects on schedule. Both receive transparent pricing, coordination with project timelines, and a documented process that protects roof penetrations and electrical connections.

The business was built to fill the gap between roofers who lack solar expertise and solar installers who don’t focus on detach‑and‑reset work. Its methodical, climate‑aware approach — accounting for heavy snow loads, freeze‑thaw cycles, and high‑altitude UV exposure — and its local, physical presence are cited as key differentiators.

All work is produced in their Menlo Park workshop using traditional joinery and finishing techniques, with each project planned around the client's specific space and requirements. The company distinguishes itself by avoiding prefabricated or flat-pack components, instead using premium materials selected for durability and daily use. Its process centers on custom planning, handcrafted construction, and a reliable workflow that aims for a precise, seamless fit in every installation.

about:
VFN Fiberglass Inc. operates from Addison, Illinois, where it has been a leader in the fiberglass automotive components industry for over 50 years. The company's founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed, but its longevity points to a stable, privately held operation.

The company manufactures a wide range of fiberglass body parts for both street and drag-racing applications. Its product line includes complete door-slammer bodies, front-end assemblies, hoods, doors, trunks, bumpers, scoops, and cowl-induction hoods. Many hoods are offered as bolt-on units designed to work with factory hinges and latches, and all street hoods are bonded with aerospace-grade adhesives. Production volumes run into the hundreds of front ends and thousands of individual panels annually.

VFN serves the automotive aftermarket, focusing on drag racers and street-performance enthusiasts. Its components are built to withstand the stresses of competition while retaining factory-style detail. Customers range from individual racers to shops building turn-key vehicles, though specific client names are not disclosed.

The business was founded on a mission to produce lightweight, durable parts that handle the abuse of drag racing without sacrificing OEM-level fit and finish. Management emphasizes that its reputation has grown through word of mouth rather than advertising, and it points to the use of aerospace adhesives as a key differentiator for product longevity.

It handles multi-component molding such as over molding and insert molding, in-mold labeling, and offers short runs through full-scale production. Standard production lead time is two weeks, with same-day shipping available for stocked items.

Customers span nutritional, nutraceutical, food, pet food, aerospace, agricultural, architectural, construction, consumer goods, dental, electrical, health supplements, marine, automotive, medical, military, oil field, optical, packaging, pharmaceutical, and transportation sectors. The company also works with inventors and new product designers from concept to shelf.

Valencia Plastics emphasizes same-day quotes, samples, and shipping, an in-house CAM-driven mold shop, ISO 9001:2015 and cGMP certifications, and the ability to process up to 100% post-consumer resin using food-grade materials.

name: Valeo
old_description: At Valeo, we strive to create a workplace based on ethics, transparency, empowerment, professionalism and teamwork. Our employees and their well-being are at the heart of our operations and we believe in creating respectful and inclusive workplaces founded on these values.
about:
Valeo's U.S. was established in Seymour, Indiana, to develop and sell thermal systems to major American automakers. The French multinational expanded through joint ventures with Eaton, Osram Sylvania, and V. Johnson Enterprises, and later acquired Blackstone and ITT Industries, solidifying its North American footprint. A joint venture with Raytheon evolved into Valeo Radar Systems, a wholly owned subsidiary. In 2017, the company added an engineering and innovation center in San Mateo, California.

Today, Valeo USA operates nine production sites, three development centers, and one service center across the country, with its regional headquarters in Troy, Michigan. Its North American plants manufacture a broad range of automotive systems: electrical systems, transmissions, engine management, air management, hybrid and electric vehicle systems, climate control, powertrain thermal systems, compressors, front-end modules, driving assistance, interior controls, interior electronics, lighting, wipers, and wiper motors. The organization is structured around three divisions—Brain, Power, and Light—focused on software-defined vehicles, electrification, and visibility technologies, respectively.

The company serves automotive original equipment manufacturers and the aftermarket through its Valeo Service division. It has earned recognition such as GM Supplier of the Year awards and participates in major industry events including the North American International Auto Show, CES, and South by Southwest.

Valeo states its mission is to make mobility cleaner, safer, and smarter, emphasizing ethics, transparency, empowerment, professionalism, and teamwork in its workplace culture.

about:
Vapos, LLC is headquartered in Jamestown, Rhode Island, and operates two processing facilities: a plant in Linden, New Jersey, and the H2O Express facility in Newman, California. The company specializes in organic pasteurization and sterilization services for the food industry.

Its core offering is contract pasteurization using two primary technologies: the proprietary H2O Express steam pasteurization system and dry-heat treatment, both designed to achieve validated log reductions at low temperatures. The company reports more than 50 validated commodities, covering nuts and seeds such as almonds, cashews, hazelnuts, macadamias, peanuts, pecans, pistachios, walnuts, and sesame and chia seeds; grains and flours including corn flour, regular flour, and treated corn flour; as well as spices, dried fruits, and pet foods.

Vapos serves food manufacturers, spice manufacturers, pet food manufacturers, and nut and grain processors. Its customer base includes participants in the almond, pistachio, and peanut supply chains, and the company regularly exhibits at events such as the ASTA Annual Meeting, the American Pistachio Growers Conference, and The Almond Conference.

The company emphasizes food safety as its mission and holds FSSC 22000 certification through SAI Global, positioning its validated processes as a way for brands to protect product integrity and meet regulatory requirements.

name: Vasoptic Medical Inc.
old_description: We specialize in the development and deployment of advanced blood flow imagers and perfusion monitoring systems.
about:
Vasoptic Medical Inc. operates from Columbia, Maryland, where it develops and deploys advanced blood flow imagers and perfusion monitoring systems. The company's founding year and ownership structure have not been publicly disclosed.

The company's core products are noninvasive optical imaging systems that capture blood flow dynamics at video rates without the need for contrast agents. These imagers are designed for clinical diagnostics and research applications, providing perfusion data that complements existing angiography methods such as OCT-angiography, fluorescein angiography, and ICG angiography.

Vasoptic's systems serve clinical settings, particularly in ophthalmology, where they assist in diagnosing vascular conditions, as well as research institutions studying blood flow dynamics. The technology generated notable interest at the ARVO 2026 Annual Meeting in Denver, indicating engagement with the vision research community.

The company emphasizes that its video-rate, contrast-free imaging offers a distinct advantage over traditional angiography by revealing real-time blood flow fluctuations over each cardiac cycle, enabling assessments that static imaging cannot provide.

They produce bespoke kitchens, walk-in closets, feature walls, offices, built-ins, and one-of-a-kind furniture pieces. All work is built in-house, from private estates in Laguna Beach and Newport Beach to commercial projects like a restaurant on Fremont Street in Las Vegas.

Clients include homeowners in exclusive neighborhoods across Las Vegas, Los Angeles, and Orange County, as well as commercial clients seeking millwork that withstands heavy use. The studio serves both residential and commercial interior markets.

The company differentiates itself through a single-team model: every project is approved via a 3D model before cutting, fabricated with CNC precision, finished by hand with bookmatched veneers and hand-rubbed finishes, and installed by their own crew. name: Vermont Green Printing
about:
Vermont Green Printing, operating as VG Printing, is a contract screen-printing and embroidery shop based in Morrisville, Vermont. The business was launched in 2014 by co-owner John Goodhue, who had spent more than three decades producing tie-dyed and screen-printed apparel for concert tours such as the Grateful Dead, Phish, and the HORDE festival, as well as wholesale accounts in the U.S. and Japan. Goodhue’s first commercial sales date back to 1983 at a Tucson street fair, and his move to Vermont marked a shift from touring merchandise to a local, service-oriented operation.

The company provides custom screen printing using water-based and algae-based inks, embroidery on caps, jackets, and fleece, full-color garment printing with a 24-piece minimum, and promotional product sourcing. Its printing process avoids plastisol and solvents, relying instead on discharge and opaque water-based inks that are free of PVC, phthalates, and heavy metals. In 2022 the shop adopted Algae Black ink, a bio-based pigment. The facility on Old Creamery Road handles both small and large runs, though specific headcount and floor space are not disclosed.

VG Printing serves a mix of regional and national clients. References on its site include Vermont Festivals LLC, the gaming brand Gamers Nexus, Riverbend Market, Green Mountain Community Fitness, the rowing-machine manufacturer Concept2, Paul’s Hardware, and the tech retailer Level One Techs. Orders range from event merchandise and corporate apparel to e-commerce fulfillment for online stores.

The company states that its founding purpose was to minimize environmental impact, pay living wages, and create products customers can feel good about. It donates at least 1% of gross sales each month to organizations such as the Vermont Food Bank, Planned Parenthood of Northern New England, The Ocean Cleanup, the Last Prisoner Project, and the Equal Justice Initiative. Goodhue’s own history — including a year in prison for cannabis cultivation — informs the shop’s support for criminal-justice reform.

about:
Virginia Diodes Inc. (VDI) is headquartered in Charlottesville, Virginia. The company was founded in 1996 by Dr. Thomas W. Crowe, who serves as CEO. It began as a spin‑off from the University of Virginia, initially selling only Schottky diodes for scientific applications such as radio astronomy and high‑frequency radar.

Today VDI manufactures state‑of‑the‑art test and measurement equipment for millimeter‑wave and terahertz frequencies. Its product line includes vector network analyzer, spectrum analyzer, and signal generator extension modules that push microwave measurement tools beyond 50 GHz. The company also produces component‑level devices — detectors, mixers, frequency multipliers, and custom systems — all built around in‑house fabricated GaAs Schottky diodes and microelectronic filter structures. Operations are housed in a 20,000‑square‑foot high‑tech facility staffed by roughly 100 engineers, technicians, and administrative personnel.

VDI serves scientific, military, and commercial markets. Early customers included radio astronomy observatories and radar programs; the portfolio has since expanded to support terahertz transmitter and receiver modules for a range of defense and research applications.

The firm’s stated mission is to make the terahertz region of the electromagnetic spectrum as useful as the microwave and infrared bands. This focus on extending measurement capability into the THz band, combined with vertical integration of diode fabrication, is presented as its core differentiator.

about:
Wabash Plastics, Inc. was founded in 1973 in Evansville, Indiana, a city on the border between the Midwest and the South. The company began as an injection molder producing parts for its sister company, Cresline Plastic Pipe Co., before expanding to serve other original equipment manufacturers. Today it operates as part of a family of plastics companies headquartered in Evansville.

The company specializes in custom injection molded components and assemblies, running more than 58 injection molding machines, many configured for two-shot and multi-shot production. Its process portfolio includes gas-assist molding, insert molding, stack molding, fan and blower molding with balancing, and in-mold labeling and applique. In-house decoration capabilities cover pad printing, hot stamping, heat transfer, roll-on hot stamping, and part marking. Assembly services range from custom cells and robotic cobots to ultrasonic, vibration, spin, infrared, and hot-plate welding, plus foam-in-place gaskets and leak testing.

Wabash serves appliance, automotive, HVAC, point-of-purchase, and consumer-goods OEMs across North America. The company emphasizes reshoring and nearshoring, positioning its Midwest location as a way to shorten supply chains and improve oversight.

Wabash cites its ISO 9001:2015 certification and a history of supplier performance awards as evidence of its focus on cost competitiveness, quality, and on-time project launches. The firm says it measures results by shortening design cycles, lowering production costs, and improving product quality.

about:
Warbler Woodworks operates from a shop in Waynesboro, Virginia, where a single craftsman designs and builds custom furniture using traditional joinery. The business began as a one-person workshop focused on handcrafted pieces for the local community and surrounding areas including Charlottesville, Harrisonburg, Richmond, and Washington, D.C.

The shop produces heirloom-quality furniture such as wine cabinets, office desks, settees, dining tables, side tables, and credenzas. Each piece is made one at a time using time-honored techniques including dovetail and mortise-and-tenon joinery, executed with a blend of hand tools and power tools. The maker selects local hardwoods — primarily black walnut and cherry, along with white oak, maple, hickory, and ash — for their grain, color, and strength.

Warbler Woodworks serves residential clients who commission custom pieces for their homes. The shop’s reach extends across the Shenandoah Valley and into the Mid-Atlantic region, with customers in Virginia’s major cities and the Washington, D.C. metro area.

The founder emphasizes that mass-produced furniture lacks the subtlety and durability of handcrafted work. By relying on traditional joinery rather than screws or bolts, and by finishing each piece to highlight the wood’s natural character, the shop aims to create furniture that tells a story and endures for generations.

about:
Warfield Electric was founded in 1974 in Upland, California. The company began as a specialist in DC motor repair and has since expanded into custom motor manufacturing and large-scale remanufacturing.

Today Warfield Electric operates as both a manufacturer and remanufacturer of AC and DC electric motors. Under the WEMOCO (Warfield Electric Motor Company) banner it builds custom DC motors for original equipment manufacturers, while its DC Connection division rejuvenates obsolete industrial motors and gearboxes. The company maintains six locations across the United States — Frankfort, Illinois; Upland, California; Conyers, Georgia; Waukesha, Wisconsin; Westland, Michigan; and Dallas, Texas — and stocks an inventory of over 10,000 motors available on an exchange basis. It produces new OEM DC motors for more than 15 global manufacturers and rebuilds drive units for brands such as Hyster, Yale, Crown, Toyota, and Raymond.

The company serves the wind energy sector with new pitch motors and remanufactured pitch and yaw motors for turbines from GE, AMD, SSB, Moog, Clipper, Adda, VEM, ABB, Lonne, AVN, and Bonfiglioli. In material handling it supplies remanufactured motors and drive units for forklifts and warehouse equipment. Additional markets include ground support equipment, agriculture, mining, airport facilities, cold storage, and brewery applications. Customers range from OEMs to independent repair shops such as Mahaffeys Electric Motor Repair and large fleet operators like Anderson Material Handling.

Warfield Electric emphasizes service, quality, and price as its founding principles. It promotes its remanufactured motors as engineered to or above OEM standards, highlights a knowledgeable on-site engineering staff, and stresses honest pricing to build long-term partnerships. The firm positions itself as the nation’s largest DC motor remanufacturer, leveraging a nationwide exchange program and the ability to produce custom motors in small quantities.

about:
Watson Furniture traces its roots to 1966 when South African-born cabinetmaker and metalworker Grahame Watson opened a small workshop on Bainbridge Island, Washington. The company relocated to a 34-acre manufacturing campus in nearby Poulsbo and has remained family-owned since 2010, when Clif and Kathy McKenzie assumed majority ownership after a 1989 partnership with Bill Haggerty and Daniel Warn. Today the business is led by Chairman Clif McKenzie, President CK McKenzie, and Board Member Kathy McKenzie.

The company designs and manufactures furniture for two primary segments: modern office environments (desks, tables, systems, and storage) and mission-critical consoles for 24/7 control rooms and emergency communications centers. Production processes include a PFAS-free, heat-cured electrostatically applied coating, polypropylene edge banding as a PVC-free standard, and thermally fused low-pressure laminate fabrication. The Poulsbo facility handles all fabrication, finishing, and assembly in-house.

Customers include corporate offices, government agencies, and public-safety organizations that require durable, purpose-built furniture for high-stakes, round-the-clock operations. The firm’s pivot to mission-critical work began in 1986 when a local emergency communications center commissioned custom consoles, establishing a specialization that now runs alongside its commercial office line.

The company positions itself as fiercely independent, rooted in its community, and focused on integrity over shortcuts.

Weidmann Electrical Technology is headquartered in St Johnsbury, Vermont. The company traces its origins to 1877, when it began as a manufacturer of electrical insulation. Today it operates as a global group with a 145-year history of innovation in transformer insulation.

Weidmann serves the energy sector, transformer manufacturers, and the railway industry, providing custom-designed solutions for traction transformers that emphasize efficiency and sustainability. Weidmann differentiates itself through its long-standing expertise in transformer insulation, a global footprint that enables local support, and a sustainability strategy aligned with the UN Sustainable Development Goals and recognized by Ecovadis ratings. Western Solar Inc was founded in 2002 in Bellingham, Washington, the seat of Whatcom County. The firm provides full‑service solar photovoltaic design, permitting, installation, and ongoing maintenance, along with energy‑storage systems, electric‑vehicle chargers, and smart electrical panels. All work is performed in‑house by a crew of electricians, roofers, and designers—no subcontractors are used. Since inception, Western Solar has installed more than 3,000 residential and commercial systems throughout Washington, drawing on nearly a century of combined team experience.

Customers range from individual homeowners in communities such as Freeland, Ferndale, and Bellingham to commercial and institutional clients. A notable project is the Fisherman’s Pavilion community solar array on the Bellingham waterfront, developed in partnership with the Port of Bellingham, Puget Sound Energy, Silfab Solar, and Cascadia Renewables. The company also collaborates with local utilities to advance smart‑home energy solutions.

Western Solar distinguishes itself through an integrated, no‑subcontractor model that covers design through lifetime service, a commitment to consumer‑protection advocacy through the Washington Solar Energy Industries Association (WASEIA), and a focus on integrity and craftsmanship rather than high‑pressure sales.

about:
Wild Springs Solar is a 128-megawatt solar project located near New Underwood in Pennington County, South Dakota. The project is developed by Geronimo Power, a renewable energy company formerly known as National Grid Renewables. Geronimo Power's headquarters are listed in New Underwood, South Dakota, though its development staff operate across the Midwest. The company's founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed in the available materials.

Geronimo Power develops, owns, and operates utility-scale renewable energy infrastructure. Its portfolio includes solar generation, battery storage, onshore wind, and what it terms Powered Data Parks—campuses that co-locate data centers with dedicated renewable generation. The Wild Springs project connects to the New Underwood Substation within the Southwest Power Pool market and represents approximately 200 construction and operations jobs. The company manages permitting, land acquisition, and community engagement through internal teams such as the permitting lead and senior project developers.

The company works with electric utilities, independent power producers, corporate offtakers, landowners, and local communities. Concrete projects referenced include the 100-megawatt Apple River Solar, the 150-megawatt Bee Hollow Solar, and the 270-megawatt Blevins Solar & Storage project with 360 megawatt-hours of storage. Geronimo Power also engages with educational institutions through charitable giving programs tied to project revenues.

Geronimo Power emphasizes a community-benefit model branded as "Solar Does Good," citing commitments such as $500,000 in charitable giving over 20 years at Wild Springs and an estimated $29.5 million in direct economic impact. The company states it operates with honesty, integrity, and respect, and maintains an ethics and compliance hotline for stakeholders.

Its portfolio spans kitchens, baths, staircases, entry doors, handrails, and built-in bookcases, often incorporating reclaimed barnwood finished with proprietary water- and stain-resistant coatings that preserve a raw appearance.

Ching attributes the firm's reputation to a team-based approach—he holds the vision but gives every employee a stake in project decisions—and to close coordination with design teams, often holding eight to ten face-to-face meetings per project to align construction with the homeowner's intent.

about:
Wolfspeed operates a silicon carbide semiconductor fabrication facility in Fayetteville, Arkansas. The company is the world's only pure-play, vertically integrated silicon carbide manufacturer, producing both substrates and power devices under one roof.

The Fayetteville site manufactures silicon carbide substrates, power modules, discrete power devices (including MOSFETs and Schottky diodes), and power die products. Wolfspeed has recently expanded to 200 mm wafer processing, introducing premium n-type SiC substrates that improve yield per wafer and per lot. The company provides design support tools, reference designs, evaluation kits, and gate driver boards to accelerate customer development. Its "silicon carbide corridor" enables end-to-end fabrication from substrate to finished device at massive scale.

Concrete examples include a partnership with Stercom to scale grid-compatible V2X technology for heavy-duty EVs, a long-term wafer supply agreement with Infineon, and collaboration with Amperesand on medium-voltage solid-state transformers for AI data centers.

Wolfspeed differentiates itself through its pioneering role in silicon carbide, vertical integration from substrate to system, and a focus on enabling electrification and sustainability. The company emphasizes safety, integrity, ingenuity, and ownership as core values guiding its operations.

about:
Xometry operates from Lexington, Kentucky, where it was founded in 2013 with a mission to make the world's manufacturing capacity accessible to all. The company went public in June 2021 and has since grown to a global team of over 1,500 employees.

The company runs an AI-driven digital marketplace that connects buyers to a vetted network of more than 5,000 manufacturing suppliers. Through its instant-quoting engine, Xometry offers CNC machining (3-, 4-, and 5-axis milling, turning, drilling, and wire EDM), a full suite of 3D printing technologies (FDM, HP Multi Jet Fusion, SLS, SLA, PolyJet, Carbon DLS, DMLS, and metal binder jetting), sheet and tube fabrication (laser cutting, waterjet, bending, and tube laser cutting), injection molding, urethane and silicone casting, plastic extrusion, die casting, metal stamping, metal extrusion, welding, and assembly. The platform has shipped over 165 million parts to 90,000 active buyers worldwide.

Xometry serves Fortune 500 companies in aerospace and defense, automotive, and medical sectors, as well as space exploration and electric-vehicle programs. Documented customer projects include helping SentriLock overcome supply-chain disruption, scaling critical components for an electric motorcycle maker, delivering precision parts for Intuitive Machines' lunar mission, supporting Sea Box on a major defense project, and contributing to the Elettra 2.0 light-source upgrade.

Xometry differentiates itself by acting as the manufacturer of record, standing behind every part's outcome. Its AI-powered quoting engine delivers instant prices with no minimum order quantities, free standard U.S. shipping, and integrated digital workflows that provide traceability and transparency from order to delivery. The company holds ISO 9001:2015, ISO 13485:2016, AS9100D, IATF 16949:2016, ITAR registration, and CMMC Level 2 certification.

name: ixana
old_description: Continuous context and feedback for wearables and edge devices, with wire-like latency at ultra-low power
about:
Ixana is headquartered in West Lafayette, Indiana. The company emerged from foundational research on electro-quasistatic (EQS) communication conducted at Purdue University between 2016 and 2020, producing its first proof-of-concept silicon in 2021. It is led by a team of mixed-signal veterans including Shreyas Sen (CTO and inventor of Wi-R), Angik Sarkar (CEO), Shovan Maity (Head of Research), and Bob Twomey (EVP Sales).

Ixana designs and ships ultra-low-power Wi-R silicon that uses localized electric fields to create a "wireless wire" for short-range, high-speed data links along a person, robot, or machine. Its production-grade XA-NFE2001 transceiver delivers 5 Mbit/s at 0.2 nJ/bit, with a 20 Mbit/s XA-NFE3001 in sampling. The company handles full-custom mixed-signal IC design, AI-accelerated tapeout cycles, silicon validation, and provides development kits to partners.

The technology targets wearable AI (smart glasses, biosensor patches), medical and biosensing systems, robotics, automotive and industrial equipment, and mission-critical defense applications. Early partners include OTTO Engineering for tactical audio and radio integration, the U.S. Air Force and USSOCOM for augmented reality programs, and unnamed Tier-1 smartphone, wearables, and platform OEMs. Research collaborations continue with Purdue University and the NSF.

Ixana was founded to break the energy-latency trade-off that limits continuous Physical AI, offering a "second nervous system" that is private by physics because the EQS field stays confined to the user's immediate space. The company emphasizes first-principles physics, 5-month tapeout cycles, and 25+ patents filed annually as its differentiators.

It serves the architectural, marine, yachting, construction, and industrial fabrication sectors, often collaborating with engineers and draftsmen to realize complex projects.

603 Metals emphasizes craftsmanship as its guiding principle, drawing on the owner’s heritage and apprenticeship under a master fabricator. 731 Woodworks is based in Monticello, Arkansas, and operates as 731 LLC, owned by Matt and Amy Outlaw. The name references July 31, 1999, the day the couple met, and the anchor in their logo reflects a personal faith reference.

A coaching program called Sawdust Startups serves a community of 500+ members with weekly live calls, templates, and a marketing playbook.

The primary audience is hobbyist and small‑shop woodworkers seeking tool buying guidance, project plans, and business coaching. Customers include beginners looking for free or low‑cost plans, experienced makers wanting curated tool deals, and aspiring side‑hustle builders who join the paid coaching tier. Industries served span woodworking education, digital product sales, affiliate marketing, and online community building.

The Outlaws position the brand on transparency and practical experience: Matt tests tools himself so viewers can avoid costly mistakes, and the coaching program is built on his own path from garage shop to full‑time creator. The faith‑inspired anchor logo and the origin story tied to their wedding date are cited as core differentiators.

A&M Plastics operates from South Houston, Texas, where Arthur and Kathy Mason founded the company in 1988. The shop runs ten injection molding presses and two extrusion lines, supported by machining, assembly, sonic welding, hot stamping, and other secondary operations. In-house mold development, engineering support, and prototyping feed into production, while warehouse space and drop-shipping services allow customers to consolidate supply-chain steps. Over more than 35 years the company has brought hundreds of products to market and shipped millions of parts.

Customers span automotive, medical, oil and gas, construction, and consumer-products sectors. Named accounts include Igloo, Parker Hannifin, Emerson, Safety Maker, and projects supporting NASA; a testimonial from Liquid Health Labs highlights quick setup and reliable delivery.

The founders frame their differentiation around the responsiveness and accountability that a family-owned structure enables, emphasizing a lean operational approach, single-source manufacturing from concept through fulfillment, and a commitment to long-term partnership over transactional relationships.

name: ADAR Technologies
old_description: Our advanced technology transforms waste into opportunity—dry, pulverize, and sanitize with zero emissions.
about:
ADAR Technologies is headquartered in Phoenix, Arizona. The company was formed in 2025 by CEO Dan Kelly, COO Doug Farrington, and Technology Advisor Arie Bos, following three years of development that began in 2022 with a prototype in the Netherlands. The founders set out to solve the problem of wet organic materials — manure, sludge, surplus produce — that were too costly to dry conventionally and too valuable to discard.

ADAR’s core technology, called ADS, dries, pulverizes, and sanitizes waste in a single pass without fossil fuels, added heat, or harmful chemicals. The process yields a dry, odorless, pathogen-free powder that retains the full nutritional profile of the source material. The company commercializes this output in two ways: it sells spec‑consistent powder ingredients — high‑protein supplements from seaweed and seafood waste, zeolite powder, and nutrient‑rich fertilizer from manure — directly to formulators and blenders in the feed, pet food, fertilizer, fuel, and mineral markets; and through ADAR Environmental Services it assumes waste streams from generators at roughly half their current disposal cost, turning liability into feedstock.

Primary customers include animal‑nutrition formulators, pet‑food manufacturers, fertilizer blenders, and industrial mineral processors. A global agricultural company has already endorsed the technology for converting sargassum seaweed and seafood waste into high‑protein livestock feed. Municipal sewage, agricultural by‑products, and wood‑chip waste are also cited as feedstocks.

The company’s differentiation rests on three claims: zero‑emission processing, 100 % nutrient retention, and a business model that cuts waste‑disposal costs by 50 % while creating salable ingredients. The founders state that no thermal process has previously achieved a shelf‑stable, pathogen‑free powder with complete nutrient integrity.

about:
Accessibility Medical Equipment operates as a non-profit in Kansas City, Missouri The organization is sustained by community donations of medical equipment and a grant from the Missouri Assistive Technology Advisory Council, which funds its equipment recycling and reuse program.

The organization collects donated durable medical equipment, then inspects, refurbishes, cleans, and sanitizes each item using a process that exceeds CDC and CMS standards, including laboratory-grade disinfectant and a 360-degree Fahrenheit commercial steam system. It sells both refurbished and new medical equipment—mobility aids, bathroom safety products, hospital beds, lifts, respiratory devices, and daily living supplies—and also provides repair services and equipment rentals.

Its customers include seniors, individuals with disabilities, people with temporary medical needs, and the organizations that serve them. The company accepts Medicare, Kansas Medicaid, and Missouri Medicaid, and imposes no purchase qualifications.

Accessibility Medical Equipment was founded on the principle that cost should not block access to medical equipment needed for recovery, independence, or quality of life, especially when gently used equipment is available in the community.
